thread:
maria: Heads-up — since ~03:00 UTC the batch queue (gpu-batch) is stuck with ~40 Pending pods, cluster isn't creating new nodes.

maria: Quick excerpt from a pending pod describe: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ---   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   5m    default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```

alex: Are those pods requesting fractional GPUs or whole GPUs?

maria: Most of them are `requests:
  nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25` — we rolled out fractional-GPU experiment on the batch workers last week to get higher utilization.

rachel: That explains it. CA usually won't scale if it can't find a node group that can satisfy the pod's request shape. If requests are fractional the autoscaler will often hit "no candidate nodegroup" logic. Check CA logs for `NotTriggerScaleUp`.

dan: We're seeing classic fragmentation/"blackhole" behavior: nodes end up with leftover 0.75/0.5 GPU slices that can't be used by new pods because the scheduler treats GPUs as scalar whole resources unless MIG/device-plugin exposes fractional allocatable.

priya: Confirmed — our gpu node images don't have MIG enabled and the device plugin on those nodes is the stock nvidia device plugin (no fractional virtualization). So kube reports allocatable as whole GPUs.

infra-bot: autoscaler-check: nodegroups inspected: [gpu-pool-prod (min=2 max=20)], pending_pods=40, scale_decision=NO_SCALE, reason="PodsNotTriggeringScaleUp: insufficient candidates because of resource shape/fragmentation"

alex: Short term mitigation options:
- change pod requests to `1` for a subset of workers so CA will trigger a nodegroup scale up (coarser but predictable)
- throttle the batch submitter to reduce new Pending churn
- mark a nodepool with min>0 to keep warm capacity (but cost rises)

rachel: Long term: enable MIG or GPU partitioning on an A100 pool + update device plugin so scheduler can see MIG profiles as separate allocatable devices. That will let us binpack fractional workloads onto single GPUs and reduce blackholes. Also consider using a custom scheduler-extender or CA patch that accounts for fractional packing heuristics.

maria: Cost note — scaling by whole nodes for 40 pods will add ~2-3 whole nodes (hours) and double cost for that job. We need a cost vs latency decision for batch jobs.

dan: Another intermediate idea: create a dedicated "micro-gpu" nodepool with MIG-enabled instances (split into 4 or 7 profiles) and set CA min=1. Put non-critical fractional jobs there. That preserves main pool behavior.

priya: I've repro'd this in staging: create 3 nodes with 1 GPU each, schedule eight 0.25-GPU pods, CA doesn't scale because there are leftover fractions but not a clean whole. When I switched pods to request `1` GPU CA scaled immediately. Logs show CA reasoning: `PodRequestedResources: nvidia.com/gpu=1 required to trigger group capacity`

alex: Action items:
- rachel to open infra ticket to audit nodepool/device-plugin config and propose MIG pool (priority P2)
- priya to run an automated MIG provisioning test on staging and paste results
- maria to throttle batch submitter and revert critical workers to integer GPU requests for the next 4 hours

rachel: I'll file the ticket now and include CA logs + sample `kubectl describe pod` + staging repro.

maria: Thanks — will monitor and update here. :thumbsup:

alex: FYI here's a quick patch command if we want to keep 1 warm node temporarily: `kubectl patch nodepool gpu-pool-prod -p '{"spec":{"autoscaling":{"minSize":1}}}'` — remember this increases hourly spend.

maria: Noted. If anyone sees immediate spike in preemptible/spot evictions after warming nodes call out here.

infra-bot: reminder: opened incident ticket #INFRA-4532 (temp) for batch-job-scale-stall (assigned rachel).
